messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT (INC-7892) - AZ9 networking: spike in 5xxs for services behind regional LB. Pager to #incidents and on-call. See alert: https://monitoring.example/INC-7892
sara-ops: getting the alert as well, looks like a sudden increase in backend connection resets, graphs show IPv6 traffic error rate up ~40% from baseline.
ashley-net: I see a lot of PMTUD ICMP 'packet too big' suppression traces on our AZ9 egress routers, and some jumbo frames are being black-holed by an intermediate provider. IPv6 path MTU probes are being rate-limited.
mike-support: multiple customers (EU media upload) reporting failures when uploading >1200B blobs. Support ticket cluster: #TKT-4521, customers complaining it times out or gets EPROTO.
devon-oncall: joining, thanks. Can someone paste a failing client-side curl/trace? want to reproduce quickly.
sara-ops: here is a failing trace from a repro box: ```
$ curl -6 -v https://upload.example/path -F file=@big.bin
* TCP_PACKETS OUT OF ORDER?
* recv: Connection reset by peer
* Received HTTP code 000 from URL, retrying...
```
ashley-net: tcpdump on egress shows ICMPv6 type 2 (Packet Too Big) being sent from our app host, but the ICMP replies never make it to the client because they're dropped at the ISP. PMTUD can't finish, so endpoints don't reduce MSS and retransmit fails.
ryan-sre: confirming, simulated MTU path contains a hop advertising 1280 but PMTUD probes suppressed. Per RFC the effective MTU should drop to 1280 but most stacks require ICMP.
leah-pm: customer impact estimate? are these all uploads or general traffic?
mike-support: primary impact: uploads and large POSTs, also some websockets sessions with larger initial frames are dropping. Currently ~23 paying customers affected, mostly EU->AZ9.
devon-oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable MSS clamping on the regional NAT/GW for IPv6 flows to 1240 to avoid fragmentation; 2) push config to route affected prefix to secondary AZ (AZ7) as fallback for new sessions; 3) add temporary traffic steering to prefer IPv4 where possible. I'll coordinate.
sara-ops: I can apply MSS clamp to the NAT gateway now. Command (applied via infra tool): ```
infractl net update --region=az9 --resource=nat-gw-12 --ipv6-mss=1240
```
ashley-net: after clamp applied I see a drop in retransmits on the egress router, initial signs look good. Please monitor error-rate graphs.
devon-oncall: stepping up routing change: adding BGP community to prefer ipv4 next-hop for affected customer prefixes: ```
bgp-policy attach community 65432:124 allow-prefer-ipv4 for-prefix 203.0.113.0/24,2001:db8:55::/48
```
sara-ops: applied. New sessions from repro box succeed over IPv6 now with clamping in place (verified upload finished). :white_check_mark:
mike-support: pushing a batch note to the 23 customers that we have an active mitigation and are monitoring. Draft: "We observed IPv6 path MTU issues impacting uploads from EU to AZ9. We've applied a temporary workaround (MSS clamping + routing preference) and are monitoring. No action required on your side." Thoughts?
leah-pm: send now, but tag customers as impacted and offer a support call window. Also track these customers for SLA credits as needed.
devon-oncall: monitoring window 30m, will keep clamp in place and watch for side-effects (tcp performance, small-packet latency). I'll keep steering enabled until we have a permanent fix with transit partner.
ashley-net: long-term: engage transit provider NOC for PMTUD probe suppression; request they allow ICMPv6 PTB or implement per-flow fragmentation handling. Also evaluate enabling Stateful PMTUD (linux kernel option) where safe.
ryan-sre: note: clamping could impact path performance for some flows — we'll record regressions and roll back if increase in small-packet latency >5ms.
incident-bot: Incident INC-7892 severity elevated to P2. On-call: devon-oncall. Pager duty: notified.
leah-pm: customer impact summary for postmortem: 23 customers affected, ~12% of sessions served by AZ9 at peak, no data loss reported, degraded uploads/timeouts for 22 minutes until mitigation applied. Assigning lead: ashley-net (network), investigation owner: devon-oncall, postmortem due in 72h.
mike-support: tickets created/linked: TKT-4521..TKT-4544. I will add affected accounts and email logs.
devon-oncall: handing off active watch to ryan-sre for next 2h while I go sleep. ryan-sre you have my notes in the runbook under INC-7892/watcher.
ryan-sre: taking watch, acknowledged. Will escalate to transit NOC if we see recurrence after clamp removal.
sara-ops: adding automatic alert: if ipv6 error-rate >15% for 5m in AZ9 re-open page.
leah-pm: thanks team — please add timeline and config diffs to the postmortem doc. We'll coordinate public customer follow-up after root cause confirmed. :hourglass:
